observations.text: EXPORT-OUTPUT is declared ORGANIZATION INDEXED with RECORD KEY EXPORT-SEQUENCE-NUM, but EXPORT-SEQUENCE-NUM belongs to EXPORT-RECORD in WORKING-STORAGE (COPY CVEXPORT), not to the FD record EXPORT-OUTPUT-RECORD; the FD also states RECORDING MODE F. A record key outside the file's record area is not valid COBOL, so the intended organization (KSDS vs sequential) needs confirmation.
Every export record is stamped with branch id '0001' and region 'NORTH' regardless of the data.
Customer SSN, government id, and card CVV are copied in clear text into the export file (CVV stored as binary COMP, which is not encryption).
6000-FINALIZE closes all six files without checking any file status.
WS-FORMATTED-TIMESTAMP (X(26)) is built from date (10) + space + time (8) + '.00' = 22 characters; STRING does not pad, so the last 4 bytes are never set by the program.
9999-ABEND-PROGRAM calls CEE3ABD with no abend code or timing parameters, unlike other CardDemo batch programs which pass ABCODE 999.

paragraphs.logic: Performs 1000-INITIALIZE, then 2000-EXPORT-CUSTOMERS, 3000-EXPORT-ACCOUNTS, 4000-EXPORT-XREFS, 5000-EXPORT-TRANSACTIONS and 5500-EXPORT-CARDS in that order, then 6000-FINALIZE, and ends with GOBACK.
paragraphs.name: 0000-MAIN-PROCESSING

paragraphs.logic: Displays 'CBEXPORT: Starting Customer Data Export', performs 1050-GENERATE-TIMESTAMP and 1100-OPEN-FILES, then displays WS-EXPORT-DATE and WS-EXPORT-TIME.
paragraphs.name: 1000-INITIALIZE

paragraphs.logic: Accepts the system date (YYYYMMDD) and time, formats WS-EXPORT-DATE as YYYY-MM-DD and WS-EXPORT-TIME as HH:MM:SS, and strings them with '.00' into WS-FORMATTED-TIMESTAMP.
paragraphs.name: 1050-GENERATE-TIMESTAMP

paragraphs.logic: Opens CUSTOMER-INPUT, ACCOUNT-INPUT, XREF-INPUT, TRANSACTION-INPUT and CARD-INPUT for INPUT and EXPORT-OUTPUT for OUTPUT. After each OPEN, when the status condition (WS-CUSTOMER-OK, WS-ACCOUNT-OK, WS-XREF-OK, WS-TRANSACTION-OK, WS-CARD-OK, WS-EXPORT-OK) is false it displays 'ERROR: Cannot open <file>, Status: ' with the status field and performs 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM.
paragraphs.name: 1100-OPEN-FILES

paragraphs.logic: Reads customer records sequentially until WS-CUSTOMER-EOF, creating one export record per customer, then displays the customer export count.
paragraphs.name: 2000-EXPORT-CUSTOMERS

paragraphs.logic: Reads the next CUSTOMER-INPUT record; a status other than '00' or '10' displays 'ERROR: Reading CUSTOMER-INPUT, Status: ' and abends.
paragraphs.name: 2100-READ-CUSTOMER-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes EXPORT-RECORD, sets type 'C', timestamp, next sequence number, branch '0001' and region 'NORTH', maps all CUSTOMER-RECORD fields into EXPORT-CUSTOMER-DATA (address lines and phones into OCCURS arrays), writes the 500-byte record (abend on bad status) and increments the customer and total counters.
paragraphs.name: 2200-CREATE-CUSTOMER-EXP-REC

paragraphs.logic: Reads account records sequentially until WS-ACCOUNT-EOF, creating one export record per account, then displays the account export count.
paragraphs.name: 3000-EXPORT-ACCOUNTS

paragraphs.logic: Reads the next ACCOUNT-INPUT record; a status other than '00' or '10' displays 'ERROR: Reading ACCOUNT-INPUT, Status: ' and abends.
paragraphs.name: 3100-READ-ACCOUNT-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes EXPORT-RECORD, sets type 'A' and the common header, maps all ACCOUNT-RECORD fields into EXPORT-ACCOUNT-DATA (balance and cash limit become COMP-3, cycle debit COMP), writes the record (abend on bad status) and increments counters.
paragraphs.name: 3200-CREATE-ACCOUNT-EXP-REC

paragraphs.logic: Reads cross-reference records sequentially until WS-XREF-EOF, creating one export record each, then displays the count.
paragraphs.name: 4000-EXPORT-XREFS

paragraphs.logic: Reads the next XREF-INPUT record; a status other than '00' or '10' displays 'ERROR: Reading XREF-INPUT, Status: ' and abends.
paragraphs.name: 4100-READ-XREF-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes EXPORT-RECORD, sets type 'X' and the common header, maps card number, customer id and account id (COMP) into EXPORT-CARD-XREF-DATA, writes the record (abend on bad status) and increments counters.
paragraphs.name: 4200-CREATE-XREF-EXPORT-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Reads transaction records sequentially until WS-TRANSACTION-EOF, creating one export record each, then displays the count.
paragraphs.name: 5000-EXPORT-TRANSACTIONS

paragraphs.logic: Reads the next TRANSACTION-INPUT record; a status other than '00' or '10' displays 'ERROR: Reading TRANSACTION-INPUT, Status: ' and abends.
paragraphs.name: 5100-READ-TRANSACTION-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes EXPORT-RECORD, sets type 'T' and the common header, maps all TRAN-RECORD fields into EXPORT-TRANSACTION-DATA (amount COMP-3, merchant id COMP), writes the record (abend on bad status) and increments counters.
paragraphs.name: 5200-CREATE-TRAN-EXP-REC

paragraphs.logic: Reads card records sequentially until WS-CARD-EOF, creating one export record each, then displays the count.
paragraphs.name: 5500-EXPORT-CARDS

paragraphs.logic: Reads the next CARD-INPUT record; a status other than '00' or '10' displays 'ERROR: Reading CARD-INPUT, Status: ' and abends.
paragraphs.name: 5600-READ-CARD-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Initializes EXPORT-RECORD, sets type 'D' and the common header, maps card number, account id (COMP), CVV (COMP), embossed name, expiration date and active status into EXPORT-CARD-DATA, writes the record (abend on bad status) and increments counters.
paragraphs.name: 5700-CREATE-CARD-EXPORT-RECORD

paragraphs.logic: Closes CUSTOMER-INPUT, ACCOUNT-INPUT, XREF-INPUT, TRANSACTION-INPUT, CARD-INPUT and EXPORT-OUTPUT (statuses not checked), displays 'CBEXPORT: Export completed' and the counters WS-CUSTOMER-RECORDS-EXPORTED, WS-ACCOUNT-RECORDS-EXPORTED, WS-XREF-RECORDS-EXPORTED, WS-TRAN-RECORDS-EXPORTED, WS-CARD-RECORDS-EXPORTED and WS-TOTAL-RECORDS-EXPORTED.
paragraphs.name: 6000-FINALIZE

paragraphs.logic: Displays 'CBEXPORT: ABENDING PROGRAM' and calls CEE3ABD without parameters.
paragraphs.name: 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM

rules.outcome: EXPFILE contains all records of the five source files.
rules.statement: The branch-migration export is a full, unfiltered extract: every customer, account, card cross-reference, transaction and card record is exported, in that fixed order (one entity type after another), with no selection criteria.

rules.outcome: EXPORT-REC-TYPE, EXPORT-TIMESTAMP, EXPORT-SEQUENCE-NUM, EXPORT-BRANCH-ID, EXPORT-REGION-CODE populated.
rules.statement: Each export record carries a type code identifying the entity ('C' customer, 'A' account, 'X' card cross-reference, 'T' transaction, 'D' card), the run timestamp, a sequence number incremented across all record types, branch id '0001' and region code 'NORTH'.

rules.conditions: Open status not '00'; read status not '00' and not '10'.
rules.outcome: Abend; partial export file may remain.
rules.statement: Any failure to open a source or export file, or any read status other than success/end-of-file, stops the export with an error message naming the file and its status and an abend via CEE3ABD.
A failed write of any export record (status not '00') aborts the whole export run; no record is skipped silently.

sme_questions.question: Is EXPFILE meant to be a VSAM KSDS keyed by sequence number or a plain sequential file? The SELECT says INDEXED but the key is not in the FD record.
Should branch id and region code be parameters instead of the constants '0001' and 'NORTH'?
Is exporting SSN and CVV in clear text acceptable for the migration file, or must they be masked/encrypted?

summary.text: CBEXPORT is a batch COBOL program that produces a branch-migration export file. It reads the customer (CUSTFILE), account (ACCTFILE), card cross-reference (XREFFILE), transaction (TRANSACT) and card (CARDFILE) indexed files sequentially and writes every record into one 500-byte multi-record file EXPFILE using the CVEXPORT layout. Each record gets a type code (C, A, X, T, D), a run timestamp, a global sequence number and constant branch '0001' / region 'NORTH'; several numeric fields are packed into COMP or COMP-3 to save space. At the end it displays per-type and total counts. Any open, read or write error abends the program via CEE3ABD.
